properties.address: St John's Church, Princes St., Edinburgh EH2 4BJ, UK

properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean base composed of Lower Carboniferous sedimentary sandstone and volcanic strata draped in dense glacial till. Primary architectural lithics comprise local pale buff-to-grey Craigleith and Hailes Carboniferous sandstones, finely dressed into ashlar masonry. Basal storeys feature polished Peterhead granite and dark igneous plinths. Historic masonry bound with lime-based mortar; road surfaces underlain by crushed basalt aggregate and reinforced concrete sub-bases.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Date-grounded phenology (September 9, late summer transitioning to early autumn): Distant incidental street trees (*Acer pseudoplatanus* and *Tilia cordata*) retain full, dense canopy volumes in deep forest green, exhibiting initial localized margin chlorosis and dry foliage edges consistent with late-season urban conditions.

properties.architectural_summary:
Rectified urban intersection at the convergence of Princes Street, Lothian Road, and Shandwick Place. 
- Right frontage: Continuous 4-to-6-storey commercial streetscape. Features early-20th-century Edwardian classical ashlar commercial blocks with giant order fluted pilasters, heavy modillion cornices, balustraded parapets, and attic dormers; adjacent modern infill displaying vertical steel-and-glass curtain walling.
- Left frontage: 4-storey New Town classical corner block with rusticated ashlar ground floor, regular fenestration grids with timber 2-over-2 and 6-over-6 sash-and-case windows, molded architraves, continuous string courses, and a hipped Scottish slate roof punctuated by dressed ashlar chimney stacks with ceramic pots.
- Distance skyline: Slender vertical spires and Italianate campaniles rendered in tooled sandstone masonry.
- Ground plane: Planar asphalt thoroughfare embedded with twin grooved steel tram rails, painted cross-hatched yellow junction markings, edged by straight granite kerbstones and broad Caithness flagstone pedestrian pavements.
